blueprint.title: A single candidate communication interface
blueprint.intro: The goal is not to stack five chat windows in one tab. It is to give a recruiter the complete, trustworthy history of one person so they can act without re-reading anything or asking twice.
blueprint.layoutSubtitle: Three panes: who you are talking to, what was said, and what you still owe them.
blueprint.flowSubtitle: Five different API shapes become one model before they ever reach a component.
blueprint.problemsTitle: Each recruiter pain point, and the thing on screen that answers it

problems.problem: The conversation jumps LinkedIn → WhatsApp → call → email → SMS
problems.answer: One chronological timeline per candidate. Each entry is labelled with its channel and direction, and an explicit marker is drawn where the conversation moved platform, with the gap in between.

problems.problem: Asking for the CV twice on two different platforms looks bad
problems.answer: Every request is tracked as a commitment with the channel it was asked on and the channel it arrived on. Start typing a repeat ask and the composer warns before you send it, with a link to the proof.

problems.problem: Context is spread over a hundred candidates and nobody remembers it
problems.answer: Search spans every channel, including call transcripts. The context rail keeps open requests, overdue follow-ups, notes and interaction history beside the thread instead of in someone's memory.

problems.problem: A channel can be unavailable exactly when you need it
problems.answer: Per-candidate channel health is first class. An unreachable channel is disabled in the composer with the reason, and the last channel the candidate actually replied on is suggested instead.
Adapters normalize each provider into one TimelineEntry model. The UI renders one shape; channel-specific detail such as subject lines, transcripts and delivery receipts is preserved on the entry.

problems.problem: Messages arrive while the recruiter is working
problems.answer: Inbound events append to the store and bump the unread count without stealing the current thread. Sends are optimistic and move through queued to sent to delivered, with retry on failure.
